sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

claims.text: Lewis et al. define RAG models that use an input sequence to retrieve text documents as additional context for a target sequence; the model has a retriever producing a top-k-truncated distribution over passages and a generator conditioned on input, retrieved passage, and previous output tokens. The paper evaluates knowledge-intensive tasks including open-domain and abstractive QA, question generation, and fact verification.

Lewis et al. call the document index non-parametric memory and the generator parameters parametric memory; their retriever uses a bi-encoder and maximum-inner-product search for top-k documents, and the generator combines input with retrieved text. Their experimental corpus is a December 2018 Wikipedia dump split into disjoint 100-word chunks, yielding 21M documents.

Lewis et al. define RAG-Sequence as using a single retrieved document for a complete output sequence and RAG-Token as allowing a different latent document for each target token; they also state that updating the document encoder requires periodic document-index updates and is costly during training.

findings: 论文中的检索—top-k—条件生成链路、两类记忆、DPR/MIPS、实验语料设置、RAG-Sequence/RAG-Token 以及索引更新成本均已独立核对。
候选将论文实验设置与生产实现边界明确区分，覆盖原理与应用场景来源问法，并满足 mechanism 题型要求。
